5. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the  facts and circumstances of the observed "along with the licenses under the Telegraph Act, 1885 for broadcasting etc. and under the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 for possessing the broadcasting apparatus, an intending television operator also requires a licence or no objection to be granted by the Ministry of Information for transmitting or receiving the contents of any broadcasting. At the same time the intending television operator also needs licenses under Section 35 of the B.T. Act, 2001 for telecommunication and under Section 55 of the Act for establishing, operating or using radio apparatus for the purpose of radio communication and for radio frequency". It has further been observed that the Ministry of Posts and 'Telecommunications is the concerned superior authority of licensing under the Telegraph Act, 1885 and Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 for broadcasting and that "the submission made by the learned Attorney General in this regard that as the petitioners have yet not obtained the prior permission/licence from the Ministry of Post and Telecommunication, the NOC dated 5.2.2002 has yet not legally become operative and as such things made, done or procured on the basis of the said incomplete and in operative NOC shall fall through deserves consideration." 

 7. It is further contended that the High Court Division failed to consider that as per term "Cha of the permission for use of satellite link frequency dated 20th November, 2008, the licence for frequency and radio equipment’s shall have to be obtained after installation of equipment’s and on submitting test report after commencing broadcasting. Learned Counsel argued, the petitioners had duly complied the said term and therefore they are legally entitled to get a licence and that in view of condition "Ka" of the said letter, it is apparent that the said memo dated 20th November, 2008 itself is a NOC. It has further been contended that the High Court Division is wrong in not giving direction upon the writ respondent No. 3 to grant formal licence in failing to consider that following the judgment of the High Court Division and the Appellate Division, BTRC extended the period of allocated frequency and they accorded its NOC for importation of DSMG machinery and pursuant thereto the petitioners imported machineries and installed Them in the TV Station and that as per Clause-C of the NOC they submitted test report after commencing broadcasting. Learned Counsel finally contended that in view of sections 4 and 5 of Bangladesh Telecommunication Act, 2001, the Telegraph Act, 1885, the Warless Telegraphy Act, 1933 and other laws promulgated have no force of law, and that the writ respondent No. 3 has been rested with absolute authority to give effect to the earlier order. 

 "Whether the petitioner is entitled in law on the grounds of promissory estoppel or legitimate expectation to a licence for broadcasting programmes having (I) obtained the No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Information by memo No.  তম/টিচ-৩/১০(৪)/৯৯/অংশ-১)/৬৩  dated 5.2.2002(PB/p179); (2) obtained the allocation of frequency from the Bangladesh 'Telecommunication Regulatory Authority (BTRC) by Memo No.  বিটিআরসি/এস,এম/৩-২৪/০২ পার্ট-১/০৮/২৯-২৯৪৫ dated 20.11.2008 (PB/p352); (3) complied with the terms thereof by importing machinery and equipment; (4) received permission for the import of machinery from BTRC by Memo No.   বিটিআরসি/এস,এম/৩-২৪/০২ পার্ট-১/২০০৮/৭৯-৩৩৯৪ dated 18.12.2008 (PB/p357);(5) completed the lest transmission for a period exceeding one year; and (6) submitted the test transmission report. 

 (I) Whether the licence required for the broadcasting television programmes is required by law to be granted under section 35 and/or section 55 of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Act, 2001 or whether the provisions relating to licenses under the Telegraph Act, 1885 and the Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 are also applicable.
